transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-28
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Samira (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Elena Novak (CTO - Mistral), Harold Kim (Head of Security), Priya Singh (Platform Eng), Daniel Ortiz (Legal)

Summary:
Brief: Discovery focused on security posture and hosting options (hosted vs dedicated vs private). Customer is evaluating implications for SOC2/ISO compliance, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs and KMS key custody. They want clear next steps for pilot and procurement timeline.

Topics covered:
- Compliance artifacts and attestations (SOC2 Type II, ISO 27001)
- SSO integration (Okta/Azure AD) and SAML flows
- RBAC and least privilege model for Redwood Console and API keys
- Audit logs: retention, export, SIEM hooks, immutable logs
- Encryption & KMS: BYOK, HSM, key rotation, cross-region keys
- Data residency and retention policies for embeddings and raw logs
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs (cost, latency, control)

Transcript:
[00:00] Samira (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. Quick intros, and then Diego will go through the tech side.
[00:18] Elena (Mistral): Hi all, Elena here. We're primarily concerned about compliance and key custody, so wanted to understand options.
[00:27] Harold (Mistral): And how audit logs look, like retention and tamper proofing, plus SSO and role mapping.
[00:34] Diego (Redwood): Great, so we'll run through Hosted, Dedicated and Private — and call out the security controls for each. Quick note, some of our docs sometimes say "Red wood" in auto transcripts, ignore that.
[00:48] Diego (Redwood): Hosted API: SOC2 attested, standard encryption at rest/in transit, managed keys by Redwood by default. Good for fast time to value but key custody is Redwood-managed.
[00:58] Harold (Mistral): Are you SOC2 Type II right now? And which scope — infra only or product?
[01:06] Samira (Redwood): Yes, SOC2 Type II for our hosted platform. We also maintain ISO 27001. We'll send the latest reports.
[01:15] Daniel (Mistral): Legal will want to see the exact scope plus compensating controls if we can't BYOK on hosted.
[01:22] Diego (Redwood): Totally. For Dedicated we offer reserved capacity with customer network isolation. Optionally you can enable BYOK where keys live in your KMS and we never have plaintext. There's a BYOK + HSM path if the customer needs FIPS/HSM attestation.
[01:38] Priya (Mistral): Fast follow — does BYOK mean we manage rotation? Are there client-side ephemeral keys?
[01:46] Diego (Redwood): You can either rotate in your KMS and we pull or we support wrapping keys so Redwood never stores unwrapped keys. We also have ephemeral session keys for short-lived process access.
[01:56] Harold (Mistral): How about Private / on-prem? If we go Private is there an audit log export and can we push logs to our SIEM?
[02:05] Diego (Redwood): Yes, Private includes log forwarding via syslog/HTTPS to your SIEM, and by default we provide immutable append-only logs with retention policies you can configure. Also supports retention export for e-discovery.
[02:20] Elena (Mistral): Is the audit trail tied to RBAC? We want per-user API-level events mapped back to our SSO identities.
[02:29] Samira (Redwood): We integrate with SAML SSO (Okta, Azure AD) and map SAML assertions to RBAC roles in the console. So you get user-level events and we store the subject in the audit log.
[02:43] Harold (Mistral): Any limits on retention? Our security policy says 7 years for some logs, though that seems long.
[02:52] Samira (Redwood): For Hosted there's a default retention (90 days for verbose logs) but we offer extended retention add-ons. For Dedicated/Private you control retention entirely; we can configure long-term cold storage exports to your bucket.
[03:06] Daniel (Mistral): Cost implications for long retention? We need a sense for ballpark.
[03:11] Diego (Redwood): Longer retention adds storage costs; for Dedicated customers we provide a pricing tier for archive export and compressed storage. We'll share the retention pricing table after this call.
[03:22] Priya (Mistral): On SSO — how granular is RBAC? Can we have a role that only does embeddings read, another for model deploys?
[03:31] Diego (Redwood): Yes, roles are granular — read-only for embeddings, deployer role, admin, billing-only; you can map SAML groups to those roles. We also have token-level scopes for API keys.
[03:45] Elena (Mistral): For our data residency constraints, we need all inference to run in eu-west-1. Is that possible on Hosted?
[03:53] Samira (Redwood): We do have region controls; Hosted can pin to regions for enterprise customers but it's more common on Dedicated/Private. We can show the regional availability matrix in follow-up.
[04:05] Harold (Mistral): What about model fallback and graceful degradation — we need guarantees incase the dedicated pool is full.
[04:12] Diego (Redwood): We support routing policies and automatic fallback to regionally compliant model variants with SLA tiers. For strict isolation needs, Private is the most deterministic. Hosted will have fallback but it may hit different latency characteristics.
[04:28] Elena (Mistral): If we do BYOK, do you log key usage events? We need to correlate key usage with inference requests for audits.
[04:36] Diego (Redwood): Yes, KMS ops are logged. If keys are in your KMS, you get the key use events from the provider (CloudTrail for AWS etc). We also emit a correlated event in our audit log that references the KMS op id, so you can trace request->key usage.
[04:52] Priya (Mistral): How are embeddings stored? They contain PII sometimes; do you encrypt per-customer?
[04:59] Samira (Redwood): Embeddings are encrypted at rest. For Dedicated/Private you can opt into per-customer encryption keys (BYOK) so each tenant's vectors are encrypted with distinct keys. For Hosted they are encrypted with Redwood-managed keys by default.
[05:14] Daniel (Mistral): From a legal standpoint, any subprocessing list? Who touches data?
[05:20] Samira (Redwood): We'll send our subprocessor list. It's in the SOC2/ISO artifacts and the DPA. We also have human review controls and explain where and when human ops may have access — typically for debugging under strict controls and with redaction.
[05:35] Harold (Mistral): Encryption in transit — TLS 1.2/1.3? Mutual TLS for Private?
[05:42] Diego (Redwood): TLS 1.2 and 1.3 supported. For Private we can do mutual TLS and client certs as an option, plus network ACLs and private link/peering.
[05:54] Elena (Mistral): About the console: can we restrict who can create API keys? We don't want devs spinning up keys broadly.
[06:01] Samira (Redwood): Yes, RBAC can restrict who can create service keys. We also have token-scoped limits and approval flows you can enable via governance.
[06:12] Priya (Mistral): Do you have any automated key rotation or secrets lifecycle management?
[06:18] Diego (Redwood): We recommend rotation in your KMS for BYOK. For Redwood-managed keys we rotate per our key management policy and can provide rotation docs and certs. We also support short-lived sessions for workloads.
[06:31] Harold (Mistral): SIEM integration — do you support JSON event format? Can we push to Splunk/Datadog?
[06:38] Diego (Redwood): Yes, we support structured JSON event exports and have native integrations with Datadog, Splunk, and SumoLogic; otherwise you can forward via HTTPS/syslog.
[06:49] Elena (Mistral): Any third-party pen tests or bug bounty programs? We need evidence of periodic testing.
[06:57] Samira (Redwood): We run quarterly pentests and have a coordinated disclosure program; we can provide a summary of recent tests and remediation timelines.
[07:07] Daniel (Mistral): On procurement — timeline wise we are aiming for a pilot in Q4, then enterprise contract in Q1. Legal will need the DPA and the encryption/KMS clauses.
[07:18] Samira (Redwood): Noted — we'll push those docs and Samira reiterated next steps.
[07:25] Priya (Mistral): For the POC, can we get a Dedicated slice with BYOK for a week-long run to measure latency and throughput?
[07:33] Diego (Redwood): Yes, we can spin up a Dedicated trial with a small GPU pool and BYOK enabled. We'll scope the metrics (p95 latency, tokens/sec) in the POC kickoff.
[07:45] Harold (Mistral): A few loose questions — backup/restore of keys, cross-region disaster recovery, and whether Redwood stores any unencrypted caches.
[07:56] Diego (Redwood): We don't store unencrypted model context in plaintext. KV caches are encrypted at rest; for BYOK configs we cannot access unwrapped keys. DR is supported via cross-region replication for Dedicated/Private per config. We'll include the DR runbook excerpt in the follow-up.
[08:13] Elena (Mistral): Anything else on your side?
[08:16] Samira (Redwood): Recap: we'll send SOC2/ISO artifacts, subprocessor list, BYOK design doc, Dedicated pricing and retention pricing, and schedule a POC kickoff. Also Diego will share the network diagram.
[08:30] Daniel (Mistral): Legal wants a draft of the KMS clause, I'll coordinate with Samira.
[08:36] Samira (Redwood): Perfect. Thanks everyone.
[08:41] Harold (Mistral): Thanks.
[08:43] Priya (Mistral): Bye.

End of transcript.
